findings.text: A folio may be linked to an object group only when it is not already charged; the caller must ensure the linkage stays stable through page lock, LRU isolation, or exclusive ownership, after which the folio accounting word holds the group pointer.
Resolving the object group for a memory group and node executes the underlying lookup inside an RCU read side critical section that is entered before the fetch and exited immediately after.
Kernel charged pages store their object group pointer together with a kernel memory tag in the page accounting word, marking the entry as kernel rather than user charged.

Kernel page charging for the block size implied by the order uses the current object group, bypasses charging for absent or root groups, and on successful accounting takes a group reference and tags the head page; the charge status is returned to the caller.

When a charged compound page is split, the head page group tag is propagated to every tail page and extra group references are acquired for the new pages; uncharged heads cause an early return. Folio splits similarly acquire references for the additional resulting folios when charging is enabled and the folio is charged, with the count derived from old and new orders.

Kernel memory online for a non root group with kernel accounting enabled turns on a global online indicator and records the group numeric identity in its kernel identifier field. Offline reparents that group list based LRU structures to its parent; root groups and disabled accounting cause early returns.

Writeback domain startup clears the domain, initializes its spin protection, arms a deferrable periodic timer, stamps a dirty limit time, and initializes completion accounting, returning the accounting status. Shutdown synchronously cancels the timer and tears down completion accounting. A memory group wrapper delegates init, exit and size change to the embedded domain.

Foreign dirty tracking reports the event, then reuses a table slot already matching the backing device and memory group identities or otherwise replaces the oldest idle slot. Reused slots refresh their timestamp lazily only after a small fraction of the expiry interval, bounded above by a short wall clock cap.

Foreign flush scans the fixed foreign record table and for each recent record without an in flight operation clears its timestamp, reports the flush, and triggers writeback by stored device and group identities with a foreign flush reason.
An alternate build of the memory group writeback hooks is inert: initialization reports success and exit plus size change do nothing.
Maximum private memory group identifier is a bit mask with low bits set up to the identifier shift width.

Private identifiers live in a global indexed store keyed by the group numeric identity. Removal erases a present identity and clears it. Release drops caller supplied references and when references drain also removes the identity and releases the associated subsystem state pin.

Lookup by numeric cgroup identity resolves the cgroup, fetches its memory subsystem state, converts that state to the enclosing memory group when present, releases the cgroup reference, and returns the group or null when resolution fails.

Per node group records own aggregated LRU vector statistics plus per CPU statistics, an object group list head, an initialized LRU vector, and a back pointer to the group, published in the group per node table. Destruction tolerates absent records, releases per CPU and aggregate statistics and the record itself. Allocation failure unwinds partial state.

LRU vector startup clears the vector, initializes LRU and cost spin protection and per LRU lists, poisons the unevictable list head to trap use since unevictable pages reuse linkage fields, and delegates remaining state setup to helpers.

Generational LRU vector startup sets a maximum sequence past the minimum generation count, records whether the feature is enabled, stamps all generation timestamps with current time, initializes every per generation type zone list, and when per node memory state exists seeds its sequence at the minimum generation count.
Swap backed LRU vector startup clears the disk swap in counter.

Group teardown releases each present per node record along with its original object group reference, then releases legacy events, aggregate and per CPU statistics, and the group itself. The subsystem free wrapper exits generational state and the writeback domain before that core teardown.

Generational exit warns if a group memory list is still linked or if any per node page counts remain populated, poisons the per node generational list linkage to trap reuse, and releases any bloom filter storage.

Group allocation obtains a cleared descriptor, allocates a private identity within the allowed range, allocates aggregate and per CPU statistics with per CPU entries linked to parent statistics and the new aggregate, allocates every per node record, initializes the writeback domain, then initializes high reclaim work, pressure notification, peak lists and lock, socket pressure timestamp with narrow word guard, legacy state, kernel identifier default, foreign writeback list and completion records, and generational list state. Any failure removes the private identity and frees partial state with an error pointer.
Generational group startup initializes the per group memory list queue and its spin protection when such state exists.

Subsystem allocation runs group allocation under the parent as active group, presets memory and swap high limits to maximum, links memory and swap counters to the parent or to absent parent for root, initializes statistics and event state and records the root for the parentless case, and enables socket and BPF static branches according to mount options. Legacy tuning inherits parent values.

Online brings kernel memory online, allocates shrinker maps while the group is visible to iteration, allocates and publishes a per node object group with root marking and reference plus saved original, starts periodic statistics flushing for an enabled root, onlines generational state, pins the private identity and subsystem state, and finally publishes the group in the private identity store. Allocation failures unwind object groups, shrinker maps, kernel state and identity with an allocation failure status.

Offline clears legacy state, clears memory minimum and low protections, cleans swap backed offline state, offlines kernel memory, reparents object groups after list LRU reparenting, reparents deferred shrinker counts, offlines writeback and generational state, drains per CPU stock, and drops the online identity pin.

Shrinker map allocation and release serialize on a global shrinker mutex. Allocation sizes a pointer table from the global maximum, allocates a node local descriptor plus its unit table on each node and publishes it with release ordering, unwinding all nodes on failure. Release and internal teardown free every unit table, free the descriptor with the matching allocator, and clear the pointer. Unit tables are sized and grown in rounded unit granularity, freeing partial growth on failure and stopping at absent entries on teardown.
Generic release dispatches to virtual free for virtual addresses and to slab free otherwise.

Generational online assigns each node LRU vector a random bin and the current global generation, then under the node LRU IRQ spin lock with an emptiness check queues the vector on the per generation bin queue and bumps that generation group count.
Setting minimum or low protection stores the new threshold and then walks from the counter toward the root recomputing protected usage from each counter current usage.

Deferred shrinker reparenting serializes on the global shrinker mutex, resolves child and parent node descriptors under that protection, and adds each child deferred count into the matching parent slot.
Generational offline rotates every node LRU vector of the group to the aged state.
Swap backed offline cleanup serializes on a global shrink lock and when the global next scan pointer equals the offlining group advances it through iteration until reaching absent or an online group.

Observed memory group state includes per node table, aggregate and per CPU statistics, memory and swap limit counters, writeback domain and foreign record table, generational hooks, shrinker maps reachable via per node records, peak lists with lock, pressure state, socket pressure stamp, kernel identifier, and cgroup subsystem linkage.

Hazards include assuming folio charge stability without holding a stabilizer, reusing or racing foreign slot timestamps and completion counts, publishing private identities before online completes, accessing per node shrinker or object group pointers without required mutex or RCU protection, and operating on poisoned unevictable or generational list heads.
